activities.title: International Outdoor Terrace
activities.description:
Location: International Terminal G, End of Boarding Area G

An absolute must-visit. This stunning outdoor observation deck gets you out of the indoor air and puts you right on top of the heavy international jets. Grab a drink, enjoy the California sunshine, and watch the world fly by.
activities.image_attribution: Derivative of "Outdoor terrace at SFO Airport 01" by Phoebe (CC BY-SA 4.0)

activities.title: Louis A. Turpen Aviation Museum
activities.description:
Location: Departures Level

Located in a space modeled after the original 1930s passenger lobby, this incredible free museum is filled with commercial aviation artifacts and historical airline memorabilia. It’s the perfect place to geek out over the golden age of flying.

activities.title: SFO Yoga Rooms
activities.description:
Locations:
• Harvey Milk Terminal 1: Near Gate C2
• Terminal 2: Between C and D Gates
• Terminal 3: Near Vending Machine Nook by Gate E6

Find your zen in these quiet, dedicated spaces designed specifically for self-reflection and stretching between long flights. Complimentary to use and completely silent.

activities.title: Cafe X Robotic Coffee Bar
activities.description:
Locations:
• Harvey Milk Terminal 1, near Gate B2
• Terminal 3 East, Departures
• Terminal 3 East, Arrivals

Watch a high-speed robotic arm precision-brew your latte! It is a fun, futuristic, and incredibly fast way to grab excellent coffee while you walk to your gate.

activities.title: Permanent Public Art Trail
activities.description:
Location: Throughout the airport

Stretch your legs and take a self-guided walking tour of SFO's world-class permanent public art collection, featuring massive murals, sculptures, and kinetic light installations scattered across every terminal. See if you can find all 165 pieces!

activities.title: Kids' Play Areas
activities.description:
Locations:
• Tree Town: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, Near Gate B18
• Kids' Spot: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, Near Gate B2
• Butterfly Wall: Terminal 2, Near Gate D15
• San Francisco Bay Area Bird Encounters: Terminal 2, Near Gate D7
• Kids' Spot: Terminal 3, Near Gate F17
• Spirogyrate: Terminal 3, Near Gate E7
• Kids' Spot: Terminal 3, Near Food Court

Traveling with kids? Let them burn off some energy before the flight at these beautifully designed, continuous interactive play structures.

activities.title: Freshen Up! (Nap Rooms & Showers)
activities.description:
Location: International Terminal, near the entrance to Gates G1 to G14

Need to recharge? For a fee, Freshen Up! offers private nap rooms ($150 minimum), hot showers ($30), ironing facilities ($5), and travel necessities. It's the perfect sanctuary during an ultra-long layover.

activities.title: SkyTerrace Observation Deck
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 2, Level 4

Head to the top of Terminal 2 to enjoy stunning 180-degree views of the busiest runways. It’s an incredible vantage point to watch heavies rotate and land.

activities.title: Compass Books
activities.description:
Locations:
• Terminal 2
• Terminal 3, near F1 Security Checkpoint

A highly celebrated, cozy staple of SFO. As the first independent bookstore in a major US airport, it feels like a neighborhood bookshop right at your gate. Browse a fantastic curation of bestsellers, deep-cut non-fiction, and local Bay Area authors instead of the typical, generic magazine racks.

activities.title: Video Arts Room
activities.description:
Location: Departures Level

Sit back, relax, and watch a rotating selection of short films and documentaries curated by the SFO Museum. It's a great way to kill time and learn something new before heading through the TSA checkpoints.

activities.title: Socola Chocolatier
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 3, near Gate E6

Pick up artisanal, handcrafted chocolates infused with unique, local flavors. An excellent stop to treat yourself or grab a premium gift.

activities.title: Sensory Room
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, near Gate C2

Designed specifically for neurodivergent travelers who may feel overwhelmed by the bustling airport environment. This quiet, secure room offers a calming escape with specialized sensory features to decompress before boarding.

activities.title: Tony’s Pizza Napoletana
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, SF Eats Food Hall

World-famous, award-winning pizza by 13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani available right in the terminal. The perfect comfort food to calm your travel nerves.

activities.title: Equator Coffees
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, SF Eats Food Hall

A staple Bay Area roaster serving up fair-trade, high-quality craft coffee. A massive upgrade from the standard airport chains.

activities.title: Kona’s by Pacific Cocktail Haven
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, SF Eats Food Hall

An outpost of the award-winning San Francisco bar, serving up incredible tropical-inspired craft cocktails. The best spot in the airport to grab a pre-flight drink. Ranked North America’s 50 Best Bars and the World’s 50 Best Bars in 2023 and 2024

activities.title: Boudin Bakery
activities.description:
Locations: International Terminal A, Boarding Area A, near Gate A3

A true San Francisco institution. You cannot leave SFO without grabbing one of their world-famous, freshly baked sourdough bread bowls loaded with hot clam chowder.

activities.title: Bun Mee
activities.description:
Locations: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, near Gate B3

Widely considered the absolute best food option in the airport. Highly praised for being flavorful, fresh, filling, and reasonably priced. Grab banh mi sandwiches, rich pho, hearty rice bowls, or excellent breakfast items like the bulgogi bun. Fantastic for vegetarians and vegans.

activities.title: Mama Go’s Filipino Cuisine
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, near Gate B18

A massive favorite for authentic Filipino food and regarded as some of the best value for your money at SFO. A casual, comforting staple to grab a warm bite before heading to your gate.

activities.title: Tomokazu
activities.description:
Location: International Terminal G, between Gates G4 and G8

A highly popular spot among airport employees. Known for excellent, comforting chicken or pork katsu rice bowls and rich vegetable curry. Pro-tip: phone in your order ahead of time here - 650.821.8899

activities.title: Klein's Deli
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 3

A highly convenient and solid stop for frequent flyers. While considered a bit pricey, they serve fantastic, hearty deli sandwiches paired perfectly with their signature tomato bisque soup.

activities.title: Foggy Notion
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 3, Boarding Area F

An offshoot of the beloved Inner Richmond boutique, this charming, eco-conscious shop focuses exclusively on sustainable, handmade goods from local Bay Area artisans. It's the absolute best place in the airport to pick up unique apothecary items, organic skincare, and beautifully crafted small gifts.

activities.title: Starbird
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, near Gate B13

Fast, fresh, and incredibly satisfying. Starbird serves up elite, crispy chicken tenders alongside a highly praised lineup of signature dipping sauces.

activities.title: Gott's Roadside
activities.description:
Location: International Terminal A, near Gate A14

A Bay Area classic known for tasty, elevated Americanized options. Their juicy burgers are excellent, but the Vietnamese chicken salad is a massive standout.

activities.title: Wakaba
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 2

A highly recommended oasis in Terminal 2 praised by travelers for offering quality sushi, comforting ramen, and decent curries at remarkably fair and unexploitative prices compared to typical airport dining.

activities.title: Burger Joint
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 2, near Gate D15

A reliable stop for great backyard-cookout-style burgers and fantastic breakfast sandwiches if you're flying out early in the morning.

activities.title: Napa Farms Market
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 2, D gates, Retail Street

An airy, artisan market environment. It's fantastic for hot, fresh food made in the back kitchen, along with an impressive selection of local California cheeses, pastries, and flight snacks.

activities.title: Koi Palace Express
activities.description:
Location: Terminal 3, Food Court near Gates F11 to F22

An incredible express dim sum choice to grab before or after a flight. Perfect for a quick, casual bite of har gow, siu mai, or roast pork buns when you're craving authentic flavors on the go.

activities.title: Post-Security Terminal Loop Walk
activities.description:
Location: Airside pedestrian walkways throughout all terminals

Really bored on a long layover? Walk a lap around the airport! SFO is uniquely shaped like a massive circle, meaning you can walk a complete, continuous loop through every terminal (1, 2, 3, and International A & G) without ever leaving the secure area. It takes about 20 to 25 minutes, and you'll be surprised by the art, food, and views you find along the way. Besides, you need to move your legs after being on a plane for so long.

💡 Pro-Tip: Just follow the overhead signs for the other terminals, but be careful not to accidentally wander out the exits or down the escalators to baggage claim, or you'll have to go through TSA all over again!

activities.title: Boarding Area B Observation Windows
activities.description:
Location: Harvey Milk Terminal 1, End of Boarding Area B

Head to the end of the concourse to experience a space that perfectly captures the spirit of the Bay Area. Set within the world's first LEED Platinum airport terminal, this calm and curated area is framed by high ceilings, comfortable furnishings, and abundant natural light—providing an exceptional, relaxing vantage point to track aircraft operations and watch approaches on the tarmac.

activities.title: Connector Bridge Viewpoint
activities.description:
Location: Secure walkway connecting Terminal 2 and Terminal 3

Stroll through this 14,000-square-foot connector to enjoy unique views of the tarmac alongside three new displays of public art from the San Francisco Arts Commission, showcasing works by Kim Anno, Carter-Lynch (Stacey Carter/Derek Lynch), and Paul Madonna. The space also reintroduces the Kadish Gallery—named for Ruth Kadish, the first woman appointed to the San Francisco Airport Commission in 1977—which features rotating photography exhibitions curated by the SFO Museum.
